land.text: Perlis, separated from Kedah by Siam as 'a separate principality' in 1842

predecessors.note: Kedah was annexed by Siam in 1821 and restored without Perlis in 1842; see the sultanate-of-kedah dossier. The page's infobox dates the Siamese vassal state under Raja Long Krok to 1839.

land.text: Perlis, among the states whose 'rights of suzerainty' Siam transferred to Britain by the treaty of 10 March 1909

successors.note: Perlis continues as a Malay state under British protection (a Resident at Arau) and later inside Malaysia; as a sovereign or tributary state the dossier ends in July 1909. Cliopatria ends the row in 1910.

capitals.name: Arau
capitals.note: The page names Arau as the royal capital and Kangar (about 100.19E 6.44N) as the state capital and largest city, and says the British 'installed a Resident in the Perlis royal capital of Arau' without a date. It does not date Arau as the capital in the 1840s.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 2,094 km2 against the infobox 'a total land area of 819 km2' (modern Perlis): ratio 2.56, beyond a factor of two. The gazetteer shows the shape is 5 cells, of which Perlis is 2 (about 506 km2); the other 3 cells (bbox 99.73-100.38E, 6.30-6.54N, the Langkawi side and one cell east) are not Perlis. The Kedah dossier says Langkawi is absent from Kedah's 1842-1910 shape and sits in this row. The Perlis page does not mention Langkawi, so the infobox fits Perlis alone and the shape draws more than the state; no opened page says whose the extra cells were, so the shape stays unchanged and unverified there (see notes).

correction.text: Years only: this shape holds 1908-1909; the Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 10 March 1909 (effective 9 July 1909) transfers 'all rights of suzerainty' over Perlis to Britain, so the 1910 year belongs to the British Colonial Empire row

keyframe_review.note: Same outline as 1842 (2,094 km2), same area caveat; Cliopatria's row runs to 1910, the dossier ends in July 1909.

region.text: Perlis, 'a total land area of 819 km2', royal capital Arau

ledger.note: 1842: Siam separates Perlis from Kedah as a separate principality, the year the Kedah sultan is restored without it. The page: Siam 'separated Perlis into a separate principality' in 1842, when 'the Sultan agreed to accept Siamese terms'. The infobox gives an earlier date, 'Vassal state of Siam governed by Raja Long Krok: 1839'.

region.text: Perlis, 'a total land area of 819 km2', royal capital Arau

ledger.note: 1842: Perlis passes from Siam's direct administration of Kedah (annexed 1821) to a principality of its own. Matches the Kedah dossier's 1842 restoration of Kedah proper without Perlis.

region.text: Perlis, 'a total land area of 819 km2', royal capital Arau

ledger.note: 1842: Perlis is a vassal state of Siam. Infobox: 'Vassal state of Siam governed by Raja Long Krok: 1839'; the Siamese separation is dated 1842 in the text. Recorded on the vassal's side.

1843: Siam appoints Syed Hussain Jamalullail as Raja, founding the line that still reigns. Infobox: 'Kingdom formed when Syed Hussain appointed as King by Siam: 20 April 1843'; the text has 'On 20 May 1843, the Siamese made Sayyid Hussain Jamalulail' the first Raja, 'which made Perlis a sovereign state'. He ruled 1843 to 1873.

region.text: Perlis, 'a total land area of 819 km2', royal capital Arau

ledger.note: 1909: Siam's suzerainty over Perlis passes to Britain. Article 1: 'The Siamese government transfers to the British government all rights of suzerainty' 'over the states of Kelantan, Tringganu, Kedah, Perlis, and adjacent islands'; signed 10 March 1909, effective 9 July 1909.

region.text: Perlis, 'a total land area of 819 km2', royal capital Arau

ledger.note: 1909: Perlis becomes a British protectorate. Treaty signed 10 March 1909 at Bangkok, ratifications exchanged 9 July 1909; the states enter the British sphere of influence as protectorates (treaty page). The Perlis page: the treaty 'forced Siam to relinquish its southern Malay vassal states'.

wars.name: Perang Musuh Bisik
wars.outcome: The Kedah supporters of Sultan Ahmad Tajuddin fought Siam 'for his restoration from 1830 to 1842'; Kedah was restored under Siamese terms in 1842 and Perlis was made a separate principality.
wars.note: Kedah's war; no Perlis land is named as fought over, so the zones are empty and no contest event is recorded.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary for Perlis; the frontier with Kedah and with Siamese Satun is approximate.

sources.title: Perlis
sources.note: Separation from Kedah 1842 (infobox 1839), Raja appointed 1843, 819 km2, Arau, the 1909 treaty, Japanese-period return to Siam (undated).

sources.title: Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909
sources.note: Signed 10 March 1909, effective 9 July 1909; Article 1 transfers suzerainty over Perlis and Kedah.

notes: Page budget 2 (Perlis, Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909). (1) Identity: the Cliopatria row 'Kedah-Perlis District' is the state of Perlis (Wikipedia title Perlis); the name keeps the slug. (2) Life span 1842..1909 follows the page and the Kedah dossier's 1909 end; the Perlis state continues under British protection, in the Federation of Malaya (accession 1 February 1948) and Malaysia, and 'was returned to Siam in World War II' as a reward for Siam's alliance with Japan (page, undated): none of this is modelled here because the Cliopatria row ends in 1910 and the pages give no year for the Siamese return; a dossier for the British protectorate period and the 1940s should come from the Malaya group. (3) The 1839 date of the infobox ('Vassal state of Siam governed by Raja Long Krok') against the text's 1842; 1842 is used for the start since it matches Cliopatria and the Kedah restoration. (4) Langkawi: the 5-cell Cliopatria shape holds Perlis (2 cells) plus 3 cells on the Langkawi side and east of Perlis; the page does not say whose they were. The Kedah dossier expects this row to hold Langkawi. Needs a page on Langkawi or Kedah before it is moved. (5) The infobox area 819 km2 is modern Perlis. (6) The Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909 also moved Kelantan, Terengganu and Kedah; their dossiers are other groups'. (7) Rulers: only Syed Hussain (1843-1873) and the present Raja are on the page, so no ruler strip is given.
